set2.q: Which examination comes FIRST in the suggested order?
opts: Direct ophthalmoscopy
That comes near the end.
Ocular pressure
That comes among the special tests.
Inspection
Correct — the order begins with inspection.
Visual acuity
That comes after inspection and external examination.
set2.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 21

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: What should you do if nystagmus is seen on lateral gaze?
opts: Refer immediately regardless
The material asks you to retest in the binocular field first.
Measure the intraocular pressure
Unrelated.
Bring the finger back into binocular vision
Correct — persistence within the binocular field is what makes it abnormal. If the nystagmus persists there, consider a neurologic condition.
Repeat the whole test with the other eye covered
Not the manoeuvre.
set2.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 63

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: When should the lacrimal sac compression test be avoided?
opts: If the patient has previously had cataract surgery on that eye
Not a contraindication it is.
If the patient is over sixty-five
Age is not a contraindication.
If the area is significantly inflamed or tender
Correct — it is to avoid it in that situation.
If the patient wears contact lenses
Not a contraindication it is.
set2.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 38

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: A BLUE sclera indicates what?
opts: Long-term steroid use
Not an association it is.
Osteogenesis imperfecta
Correct — the association for blue sclerae.
Liver disease
That gives a yellow sclera.
Thyroid eye disease
Not associated with scleral colour here.
set2.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 43

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: Eye pain with PHOTOPHOBIA suggests what?
opts: Inflammation of the iris
Correct — the pairing for photophobia.
Corneal abrasion
That is signalled by pain with blinking.
Temporal arteritis
That gives temporal pain.
Conjunctivitis
That gives a gritty feeling.

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: What does the cover-uncover test reveal?
opts: A slight muscle imbalance not otherwise seen
Correct — the stated purpose.
An afferent pupillary defect of the optic nerve
That is the swinging light test.
A refractive error
That is the pinhole test.
A field defect
That is confrontation testing.

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: On the red-eye chart, what is the CORNEA like in glaucoma?
opts: Steamy and cloudy
Correct — the chart's glaucoma column.
Clear
That is conjunctivitis and subconjunctival haemorrhage.
Clear or slightly clouded
That is acute iritis.
Changes depending on the cause
That is corneal injury or infection.

set2.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
set2.q: What is the correct technique for everting the upper lid to search for a foreign body?
opts: Ask the patient to look up and relax, then pull the upper lid directly upward
Looking up defeats the eversion; it is downgaze.
Press on the globe itself to push the lid outward
It is explicitly not to press on the eyeball.
Use a cotton bud placed at the lid margin itself
The material places the stick at least 1 cm above the margin.
Ask the patient to look down and relax

Correct — the step-by-step, including the 1 cm landmark. Raise the lid slightly so the lashes protrude, grasp the lashes and pull down and forward, then place a stick at least 1 cm above the lid margin at the upper border of the tarsal plate and push down as you raise the lid edge.
